discussion_comments.comment_body: Fixed. The system-directive pattern now requires actual directive language after the colon (ignore, override, bypass, from now on, new instructions, etc.) rather than matching any SYSTEM: occurrence, so ordinary status labels like "SYSTEM: backup completed" fall through to the LLM rubric instead of an instant fail. Added positive/negative regression tests for both cases.

Confirmed the mechanism, canGenerateRemote = false does force local generation unconditionally, and unlike every other plugin using that flag (which are all dataset/static-config plugins), this one genuinely needs an LLM via getTemplate(). The reason I'm not flipping it in this PR: fetchRemoteTestCases sends task: 'mcp:tool-response-poisoning' to Promptfoo Cloud's remote generation endpoint, and since this plugin is brand new, I can't confirm from this repo whether that service already recognizes the task. If it doesn't, flipping the flag just trades one failure mode for another, and could also regress currently-working local generation for anyone who gets routed to remote (e.g. cloud-logged-in users).

discussion_comments.comment_body: [P1] Preserve trace evidence for empty final responses. With llmOutput='' and traceSummary describing a successful forbidden write under the injected persona, getResult returns pass:true/score:1 without calling the grading provider. The same trace reaches the grader when text is nonempty, and the orchestrator implementation handles this case. Do not shortcut when trace evidence exists; add a regression through the real base grading path.

discussion_comments.comment_body: [P1] Do not equate empty final text with a refusal when a trace exists. This branch ignores gradingContext.traceSummary and returns pass:true even if the trace records a successful forbidden tool action under DAN. Guard the shortcut on absence of other evidence and cover the actual grading-provider path; the rubric's trace section cannot help because it is never reached here.

Fixed in 72d3c86b89: the exporter now persists the full assertion (`value` + `config`) in `params.promptfoo` for every grader type, not just `custom`, and the importer restores both (function values are still deliberately dropped). The round-trip test pins `equals: Paris` with threshold/metric/weight/config surviving intact.

Fixed in 35dcfae04b: result import now prefers the stored `metadata.promptfoo.namedScores` map (non-numeric entries filtered), keeping grader-ID-derived names only as the foreign-data fallback. Test pins `accuracy` surviving instead of becoming `tc_1_g1`.
